en: The Two Past Triads, Hetuduka (The Pair on Causes)
A past state that is neither-root (na-anahetu) is a condition, by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya), for a present state that is not-root.
A future state that is neither-root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a present state that is not-root.
Past states that are neither-root and future states that are neither-root are conditions, by way of root-condition, for a present state that is not-root.
Conditioned by root-condition. (Abbreviated. Three with respect to root;
six with respect to object and predominance; three with respect to proximity … pe … six with respect to decisive support … pe … three with respect to non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that has a non-past object and is not a root, a state that has a past object and is a root arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to cause, there are seventeen; with respect to object, seventeen; with respect to predominance, nine … pe … with respect to prenascence and repetition, nine … pe … with respect to non-disappearance, seventeen.
